title: Incidence and severity of depression in patients with primary brain tumors and their primary caregivers throughout the disease course
summary:
Background
The diagnosis of a primary brain tumor represents a major change in the lives of both the affected person and their family. In addition to the physical effects of the disease and the burden associated with surgery, radiation therapy, or medical treatment, considerable psychological distress may occur. This may include anxiety, feelings of helplessness, uncertainty about the future, and symptoms of depression.
People differ in how they cope with such a challenging life situation. Some are better able to cope with the psychological burden associated with the disease than others. Personal characteristics and the social environment may play an important role in this process. These include, for example, optimism, confidence in one's own abilities, and the feeling of being supported by other people.
However, a brain tumor affects not only the person diagnosed with the disease. The person who provides most of the care and support may also experience considerable physical and psychological strain as a result of the disease and its course. At the same time, the well-being of the caregiver may influence how the affected person copes with the disease and its treatment.

Research question
The aim of this study is to investigate how frequently and to what extent symptoms of depression occur in patients with primary brain tumors and in their primary caregivers, and how these symptoms change over the course of the disease.
In addition, the study aims to identify personal and social factors that may help patients and caregivers cope with the psychological burden of the disease. Of particular interest is whether the psychological well-being of patients and their caregivers is related and whether they may influence each other over the course of the disease. The study will also investigate whether specific characteristics of the tumor are associated with the occurrence and severity of depressive symptoms.

Methods
The study will include patients with primary brain tumors and one person close to each patient who is primarily involved in their care and support. Both patients and their primary caregivers will complete standardized questionnaires at several predefined time points during the course of the disease.
The first assessment will take place shortly after surgery. Further assessments will be performed at three, six, nine, and twelve months. The questionnaires will assess, among other aspects, symptoms of depression, coping with stressful situations, personal strengths, and perceived social support. In addition, caregivers will be asked to provide their own assessment of the patient's depressive symptoms.
By comparing the questionnaire results at the different time points, the study aims to investigate how psychological distress develops in both patients and caregivers over the course of the disease, which factors are associated with better psychological coping, and how the well-being of patients and their caregivers is related.

interventions.name: Patients with primary brain tumors and their primary caregivers will be assessed using standardized questionnaires regarding their current psychological well-being on postoperative day 3 and at 3, 6, 9, and 12 months after surgery.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Primary brain tumor (meningioma or WHO grade I–IV glioma)
- Newly diagnosed disease
- Provision of informed consent to participate in the study and capacity to provide informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
- Known psychiatric diagnosis (ICD-10 F-category diagnosis)
- Known history of tumor disease
- Age < 18 years
- Glioma or meningioma not confirmed by histopathological examination
- Lack of capacity to provide informed consent
- Insufficient proficiency in German
- Pregnancy
